title: Three-year funding deal for THEMUSEUM
subtitle: Also: procurement threshold changes, 2026 election voting methods, heritage designations, a music festival noise exemption and a Tree Cities award.
overview: Council approved a conditional three-year funding agreement for THEMUSEUM, providing up to $300,000 a year in additional funding from July 2025 to June 2028 {{vote:m2}}. The agreement brings more reporting and oversight, including a Council member and a non-voting staff member on the museum's board. Council also extended the museum's timeline to renovate and expand into 2 King Street West to the end of 2031. The funding is meant to support the downtown and a key cultural institution.

Council also changed the Procurement By-law to align with Canadian Free Trade Agreement thresholds, which expands the room for buying local and Canadian goods and services {{vote:m21}}. It reaffirmed vote tabulators and approved alternative voting methods for the 2026 municipal election {{vote:m12}}, and endorsed the scope for a Municipal Newcomer Strategy {{vote:m10}}.

Residents will also see a noise exemption for the Songscape Music Festival at the Kitchener Auditorium on June 20 and 21 {{vote:m1}}. Council moved the April 28 meeting to May 5 because of the federal election {{vote:m17}}, and the City was recognized as a Tree City of the World.

decisions.detail: Council authorized a conditional three-year agreement for up to $300,000 a year in added funding, appointed a Councillor and a non-voting staff member to the museum board, and extended the 2 King Street West expansion deadline to December 31, 2031.
Council amended the Procurement By-law to align with Canadian Free Trade Agreement thresholds and allow expanded procurement of local and Canadian goods, services and construction.
Council reaffirmed vote tabulators for the 2026 election, authorized alternative voting methods, directed a by-law, and increased the election reserve contribution.
Council granted a noise exemption for the festival on June 20 and 21, 2025 from 5pm to 11pm, with sound checks earlier in the day, subject to conditions including a pay-duty Noise Officer.
Council endorsed using the community parameters and technical evaluation criteria to guide further engagement on approaches to growth.
Council extended the corporate printing agreement for tax, utility and miscellaneous bills with the current vendor for three years, with no renewal options.
Council endorsed the scope and approach for developing the Municipal Newcomer Strategy.
Council directed staff to proceed with Option 2 for the committee structure and to prepare the policy or by-law before June 2025.

debate: Councillors questioned how the museum's next three years would differ from the last two. Museum representatives said the programming model is sound and the problem is revenue. They said the funds would pay for marketing and a development staff member to raise donations and sponsorships.

Several councillors said the Region of Waterloo should do more, noting its museum grant has been flat since 2016 while the City and the City of Waterloo have added growth allocations. One councillor asked for an exit clause if regional funding is withdrawn. Staff said annual review, quarterly financial reporting and board seats would let the City act on funding changes, and that the City would not add more money beyond this agreement.

Some councillors said they backed the funding but wanted the museum's operating model to change and for it to become self-sustaining. One did not want it to return for more money in three years. Another asked staff to consider backup plans for the building if the museum proves unsustainable.

Staff said downtown office vacancy is high and student numbers have fallen. They argued that cultural amenities like the museum help bring people downtown, and that the museum supports the nearby Conrad Centre.

On the procurement threshold change, one councillor worried about the larger delegated sole-source authority. Staff said sole sourcing is rare, items above the limit return to Council, and quarterly reports would let Council review its use.
